purpose: Machine-readable candlestick pattern specifications. This file teaches the explanation layer what a detected pattern means; engine/patterns.py decides whether the pattern exists. The prose here is not executable.

global_rules.trend_filter: Bullish reversal patterns need a prior decline or a range; bearish reversal patterns need a prior advance or a range. Continuation patterns need trend alignment.
global_rules.volume_filter: The confirmation candle should trade at or above 1.5x the 20-day average volume.
global_rules.location_filter: The pattern must sit at support, resistance, a moving average, or a range boundary. A pattern in the middle of nowhere is noise.
no_trade_if: pattern forms against a strong trend without confirmation
volume dries up on the confirmation candle
earnings or a corporate action falls inside the holding horizon
stock is in the F&O ban list
circuit limit was hit in the last 3 sessions
spread is wider than 0.5% of price

patterns.name: Doji
patterns.structure: Open and close are almost equal; body is at most 10% of the high-low range.
patterns.psychology: Buyers and sellers finished the session at the same price. Neither side could hold control.
patterns.signal: Indecision. It is a pause, not a trade signal by itself.
patterns.entry: Wait for the next candle to break the doji high or low.
patterns.stop: Other side of the doji range after the break.
confirmation: next candle closes outside the doji range
volume expands on the break
patterns.false_signal: A doji in a quiet range produces many false breaks. A doji in the middle of a trend is usually continuation, not reversal.
patterns.notes: The doji is a location marker. Its value comes from where it appears, not from the shape alone.

patterns.name: Dragonfly Doji
patterns.structure: Open, high and close are almost equal; a long lower wick dominates the range.
patterns.psychology: Sellers pushed price sharply lower, but buyers absorbed the supply and closed the session at the high.
patterns.signal: Bullish rejection of lower prices, strongest after a decline or at support.
patterns.entry: Above the dragonfly high on the next candle.
confirmation: next candle closes above the dragonfly high
volume >= 1.3x 20D average
patterns.false_signal: Fails when the next candle opens below the dragonfly low; that turns the rejection into a continuation down.
patterns.notes: Shape is identical to a hammer with a very small body. Treat it as the same rejection idea.

patterns.name: Gravestone Doji
patterns.structure: Open, low and close are almost equal; a long upper wick dominates the range.
patterns.psychology: Buyers pushed price sharply higher, but sellers took control and closed the session at the low.
patterns.signal: Bearish rejection of higher prices, strongest after an advance or at resistance.
patterns.entry: Below the gravestone low on the next candle.
confirmation: next candle closes below the gravestone low
volume >= 1.3x 20D average
patterns.false_signal: Fails when the next candle opens above the gravestone high; that turns the rejection into a continuation up.
patterns.notes: Shape is identical to a shooting star with a very small body.

patterns.name: Hammer
patterns.structure: Small body in the upper part of the range; lower wick at least 2x the body; little or no upper wick.
patterns.psychology: Sellers drove price down intraday, but buyers absorbed the supply and pushed the close back near the high.
patterns.signal: Potential bullish reversal after a decline.
patterns.entry: Above the hammer high on the next candle.
confirmation: next candle closes above the hammer high
volume >= 1.3x 20D average
patterns.false_signal: A hammer in a strong downtrend is often a pause before another leg down. No volume means no evidence.
patterns.notes: Same shape as hanging man; the preceding trend decides the label.

patterns.name: Hanging Man
patterns.structure: Small body in the upper part of the range; lower wick at least 2x the body; little or no upper wick.
patterns.psychology: Sellers tested lower prices during an advance. Buyers recovered the close, but the intraday weakness is the first crack.
patterns.signal: Potential bearish reversal after an advance.
patterns.entry: Below the hanging man low on the next candle.
confirmation: next candle closes below the hanging man low
volume expands on the down candle
patterns.false_signal: Very common false reversal in strong uptrends. Needs a lower high or a broken short-term support to matter.
patterns.notes: Same shape as hammer; only the preceding advance makes it a hanging man.

patterns.name: Inverted Hammer
patterns.structure: Small body in the lower part of the range; upper wick at least 2x the body; little or no lower wick.
patterns.psychology: Buyers tested higher prices. Sellers pushed the close back down, but the failed rally shows buyers are active.
patterns.signal: Potential bullish reversal after a decline, weaker than a hammer.
patterns.entry: Above the inverted hammer high on the next candle.
confirmation: next candle closes above the inverted hammer high
volume >= 1.3x 20D average
patterns.false_signal: Without a strong close above the high, it is just an intraday rally that failed.
patterns.notes: Same shape as shooting star; the preceding trend decides the label.

patterns.name: Shooting Star
patterns.structure: Small body in the lower part of the range; upper wick at least 2x the body; little or no lower wick.
patterns.psychology: Buyers pushed price higher, but sellers rejected the move and closed the session near the low.
patterns.signal: Potential bearish reversal after an advance.
patterns.entry: Below the shooting star low on the next candle.
confirmation: next candle closes below the shooting star low
volume expands on the down candle
patterns.false_signal: Fails in a strong uptrend when buyers immediately reclaim the high. Needs follow-through.
patterns.notes: Same shape as inverted hammer; only the preceding advance makes it a shooting star.

patterns.name: Bullish Marubozu
patterns.structure: Long green body with negligible upper and lower wicks; body is at least 90% of the range.
patterns.psychology: Buyers controlled the session from open to close. Sellers never mounted a meaningful counter-attack.
patterns.signal: Strong bullish conviction; continuation or breakout confirmation.
patterns.entry: Above the marubozu high, or on a shallow pullback that holds the body midpoint.
confirmation: volume >= 1.5x 20D average
close above nearby resistance
patterns.false_signal: A marubozu into resistance can be an exhaustion candle. Chasing the close is how traders buy the high.
patterns.notes: Best used as a confirmation candle, not as a standalone entry.

patterns.name: Bearish Marubozu
patterns.structure: Long red body with negligible upper and lower wicks; body is at least 90% of the range.
patterns.psychology: Sellers controlled the session from open to close. Buyers never mounted a meaningful counter-attack.
patterns.signal: Strong bearish conviction; continuation or breakdown confirmation.
patterns.entry: Below the marubozu low, or on a shallow bounce that fails at the body midpoint.
confirmation: volume >= 1.5x 20D average
close below nearby support
patterns.false_signal: A marubozu into support can be capitulation. Shorting the close is how traders sell the low.
patterns.notes: Best used as a confirmation candle, not as a standalone entry.

patterns.name: Spinning Top
patterns.structure: Small body between 10% and 30% of the range, with upper and lower wicks each at least 20% of the range.
patterns.psychology: Both sides moved price, but neither could hold the close. Volatility without conviction.
patterns.signal: Indecision or pause. Wait for the range to break.
patterns.entry: Break of the spinning top high or low.
patterns.stop: Other side of the spinning top range.
confirmation: next candle closes outside the range
volume expands on the break
patterns.false_signal: Frequent in choppy ranges. The break often reverses within two sessions.
patterns.notes: A spinning top after a long trend can mark a pause; it is not a reversal by itself.

patterns.name: Bullish Pin Bar
patterns.structure: Lower wick at least 66% of the range; body at most 34% of the range; upper wick small.
patterns.psychology: Price was rejected sharply from lower levels. The long wick is the footprint of absorbed selling.
patterns.signal: Bullish rejection, strongest at support or after a decline.
patterns.entry: Above the pin bar high on the next candle.
confirmation: next candle closes above the pin bar high
volume >= 1.3x 20D average
patterns.false_signal: A pin bar in the middle of a range is noise. Location is the edge.
patterns.notes: A broader version of the hammer. The detector suppresses it when a hammer or doji already fired on the same bar.

patterns.name: Bearish Pin Bar
patterns.structure: Upper wick at least 66% of the range; body at most 34% of the range; lower wick small.
patterns.psychology: Price was rejected sharply from higher levels. The long upper wick is the footprint of absorbed buying.
patterns.signal: Bearish rejection, strongest at resistance or after an advance.
patterns.entry: Below the pin bar low on the next candle.
confirmation: next candle closes below the pin bar low
volume >= 1.3x 20D average
patterns.false_signal: A pin bar in the middle of a range is noise. Location is the edge.
patterns.notes: A broader version of the shooting star. The detector suppresses it when a shooting star or doji already fired on the same bar.

patterns.name: Bullish Belt Hold
patterns.structure: Green candle that opens at or near the low and closes near the high; body at least 70% of the range; almost no lower wick.
patterns.psychology: Buyers stepped in at the open and never let price trade below it. The session was one-sided.
patterns.signal: Bullish momentum, often the first candle of a reversal or breakout.
patterns.entry: Above the belt hold high on the next candle.
confirmation: next candle holds above the belt hold open
volume >= 1.3x 20D average
patterns.false_signal: A belt hold into resistance can be a one-day squeeze. Needs follow-through.
patterns.notes: A weaker cousin of the bullish marubozu. The detector suppresses it when a marubozu already fired.

patterns.name: Bearish Belt Hold
patterns.structure: Red candle that opens at or near the high and closes near the low; body at least 70% of the range; almost no upper wick.
patterns.psychology: Sellers stepped in at the open and never let price trade above it. The session was one-sided.
patterns.signal: Bearish momentum, often the first candle of a reversal or breakdown.
patterns.entry: Below the belt hold low on the next candle.
confirmation: next candle holds below the belt hold open
volume >= 1.3x 20D average
patterns.false_signal: A belt hold into support can be a one-day shakeout. Needs follow-through.
patterns.notes: A weaker cousin of the bearish marubozu. The detector suppresses it when a marubozu already fired.

patterns.name: Bullish Engulfing
patterns.structure: First candle bearish; second candle bullish; second body completely covers the first body; second body is larger.
patterns.psychology: Sellers had control, then buyers reversed the entire prior session and closed above its open. Control changed hands.
patterns.signal: Bullish reversal, strongest after a decline or at support.
patterns.entry: Above the engulfing candle high.
confirmation: volume >= 1.5x 20D average on the engulfing candle
next candle holds above the engulfing open
patterns.false_signal: An engulfing candle in a strong downtrend is often a dead-cat bounce. Fails if the next candle closes below the two-candle low.
patterns.notes: One of the more reliable two-candle reversal patterns, but only with location and volume.

patterns.name: Bearish Engulfing
patterns.structure: First candle bullish; second candle bearish; second body completely covers the first body; second body is larger.
patterns.psychology: Buyers had control, then sellers reversed the entire prior session and closed below its open. Control changed hands.
patterns.signal: Bearish reversal, strongest after an advance or at resistance.
patterns.entry: Below the engulfing candle low.
confirmation: volume >= 1.5x 20D average on the engulfing candle
next candle holds below the engulfing open
patterns.false_signal: A bearish engulfing in a strong uptrend is often a shakeout. Fails if the next candle closes above the two-candle high.
patterns.notes: One of the more reliable two-candle reversal patterns, but only with location and volume.

patterns.name: Piercing Line
patterns.structure: First candle bearish; second candle bullish; second opens below the first close and closes above the midpoint of the first body but below its open.
patterns.psychology: Sellers extended the decline, but buyers pushed the close deep into the prior body. The prior down move is losing force.
patterns.signal: Bullish reversal after a decline.
patterns.entry: Above the piercing candle high.
confirmation: volume >= 1.3x 20D average on the second candle
next candle holds above the piercing close
patterns.false_signal: If the second close only reaches the midpoint, it is a weak bounce, not a piercing line.
patterns.notes: A less aggressive version of the bullish engulfing.

patterns.name: Dark Cloud Cover
patterns.structure: First candle bullish; second candle bearish; second opens above the first close and closes below the midpoint of the first body but above its open.
patterns.psychology: Buyers extended the advance, but sellers pushed the close deep into the prior body. The prior up move is losing force.
patterns.signal: Bearish reversal after an advance.
patterns.entry: Below the dark cloud candle low.
confirmation: volume >= 1.3x 20D average on the second candle
next candle holds below the dark cloud close
patterns.false_signal: If the second close only reaches the midpoint, it is a weak pullback, not a dark cloud cover.
patterns.notes: A less aggressive version of the bearish engulfing.

patterns.name: Bullish Harami
patterns.structure: First candle bearish and large; second candle bullish and small, with its body inside the first body.
patterns.psychology: The large down candle showed seller control. The small inside candle shows sellers could not extend the move; the market is pausing.
patterns.signal: Potential bullish reversal, weaker than an engulfing.
patterns.entry: Above the first candle high, or above the second candle high for a faster entry.
confirmation: next candle closes above the first candle open
volume expands on the confirmation
patterns.false_signal: A harami is a pause, not a reversal. Without a strong confirmation candle it often continues down.
patterns.notes: The inside body is the key. If the second body is not inside the first, it is not a harami.

patterns.name: Bearish Harami
patterns.structure: First candle bullish and large; second candle bearish and small, with its body inside the first body.
patterns.psychology: The large up candle showed buyer control. The small inside candle shows buyers could not extend the move; the market is pausing.
patterns.signal: Potential bearish reversal, weaker than an engulfing.
patterns.entry: Below the first candle low, or below the second candle low for a faster entry.
confirmation: next candle closes below the first candle open
volume expands on the confirmation
patterns.false_signal: A harami is a pause, not a reversal. Without a strong confirmation candle it often continues up.
patterns.notes: The inside body is the key. If the second body is not inside the first, it is not a harami.

patterns.name: Tweezer Bottom
patterns.structure: Two consecutive candles with nearly equal lows; the first bearish and the second bullish.
patterns.psychology: Sellers tested the same low twice and failed to break it. The double rejection builds a support level.
patterns.signal: Bullish reversal at support.
patterns.entry: Above the two-candle high.
confirmation: next candle closes above the two-candle high
volume >= 1.3x 20D average
patterns.false_signal: Equal lows inside a downtrend are often a pause before a fresh breakdown. Needs a higher low to confirm.
patterns.notes: The two lows must be close relative to the recent range, not just numerically equal.

patterns.name: Tweezer Top
patterns.structure: Two consecutive candles with nearly equal highs; the first bullish and the second bearish.
patterns.psychology: Buyers tested the same high twice and failed to break it. The double rejection builds a resistance level.
patterns.signal: Bearish reversal at resistance.
patterns.entry: Below the two-candle low.
confirmation: next candle closes below the two-candle low
volume >= 1.3x 20D average
patterns.false_signal: Equal highs inside an uptrend are often a pause before a fresh breakout. Needs a lower high to confirm.
patterns.notes: The two highs must be close relative to the recent range, not just numerically equal.

patterns.name: Inside Bar
patterns.structure: The second candle's high is at or below the first high, and its low is at or above the first low.
patterns.psychology: Volatility contracted. The market is coiling inside the prior session's range.
patterns.signal: Compression before a breakout. Direction is unknown until the range breaks.
patterns.entry: Break of the mother bar high or low.
patterns.stop: Other side of the mother bar.
confirmation: close outside the mother bar range
volume expands on the break
patterns.false_signal: Inside bars are common; most breakouts fail in a range. Trade only with trend and volume.
patterns.notes: Also called a mother bar / inside bar setup. NR7 is a related volatility-contraction idea.

patterns.name: Outside Bar
patterns.structure: The second candle's high is above the first high and its low is below the first low.
patterns.psychology: Volatility expanded in both directions. One side eventually won the session.
patterns.signal: Expansion. The close tells you which side won.
patterns.entry: Break of the outside bar high or low in the direction of the close.
patterns.stop: Other side of the outside bar.
confirmation: close in the upper or lower third of the bar
volume >= 1.5x 20D average
patterns.false_signal: A outside bar with a close in the middle is a two-sided trap. No trade.
patterns.notes: The detector labels it neutral; the signal layer must use the close location to pick a side.

patterns.name: Bullish Kicker
patterns.structure: First candle bearish; second candle bullish and opens above the first candle high; second body is strong.
patterns.psychology: Sentiment flipped overnight. Sellers were trapped and buyers gapped price above the prior session.
patterns.signal: Strong bullish reversal or continuation gap.
patterns.entry: Above the kicker candle high, or on the first shallow pullback that holds the gap.
patterns.stop: Below the kicker candle low, or below the gap.
confirmation: gap holds for the next 2 sessions
volume >= 1.5x 20D average
patterns.false_signal: Gaps fill often. A kicker without follow-through becomes a failed gap.
patterns.notes: One of the stronger two-candle signals because it requires a gap, not just a body reversal.

patterns.name: Bearish Kicker
patterns.structure: First candle bullish; second candle bearish and opens below the first candle low; second body is strong.
patterns.psychology: Sentiment flipped overnight. Buyers were trapped and sellers gapped price below the prior session.
patterns.signal: Strong bearish reversal or continuation gap.
patterns.entry: Below the kicker candle low, or on the first shallow bounce that fails at the gap.
patterns.stop: Above the kicker candle high, or above the gap.
confirmation: gap holds for the next 2 sessions
volume >= 1.5x 20D average
patterns.false_signal: Gaps fill often. A kicker without follow-through becomes a failed gap.
patterns.notes: One of the stronger two-candle signals because it requires a gap, not just a body reversal.

patterns.name: Morning Star
patterns.structure: First candle bearish and strong; second candle small and gapped below the first close; third candle bullish and closes above the midpoint of the first body.
patterns.psychology: Sellers dominated, then momentum stalled, then buyers reversed the move. The three sessions show a handover of control.
patterns.signal: Bullish reversal after a decline.
patterns.entry: Above the third candle high.
confirmation: third candle closes above the first body midpoint
volume >= 1.5x 20D average on the third candle
patterns.false_signal: If the third candle closes below the first midpoint, the reversal is weak. A morning star inside a strong downtrend often fails.
patterns.notes: The gap is not mandatory on all timeframes, but it strengthens the pattern.

patterns.name: Evening Star
patterns.structure: First candle bullish and strong; second candle small and gapped above the first close; third candle bearish and closes below the midpoint of the first body.
patterns.psychology: Buyers dominated, then momentum stalled, then sellers reversed the move. The three sessions show a handover of control.
patterns.signal: Bearish reversal after an advance.
patterns.entry: Below the third candle low.
confirmation: third candle closes below the first body midpoint
volume >= 1.5x 20D average on the third candle
patterns.false_signal: If the third candle closes above the first midpoint, the reversal is weak. An evening star inside a strong uptrend often fails.
patterns.notes: The mirror of the morning star.

patterns.name: Three White Soldiers
patterns.structure: Three consecutive bullish candles, each closing higher than the prior close, each opening at or above the prior open, with strong bodies.
patterns.psychology: Buyers showed up three sessions in a row and closed near the highs. Selling pressure is absent.
patterns.signal: Bullish continuation or reversal confirmation.
patterns.entry: Above the third candle high, or on a pullback that holds the first candle midpoint.
confirmation: volume stays above average across the three candles
no long upper wicks
patterns.false_signal: Three strong candles into resistance can be exhaustion. Chasing the third close is late.
patterns.notes: Best after a base or a pullback, not after a long extended run.

patterns.name: Three Black Crows
patterns.structure: Three consecutive bearish candles, each closing lower than the prior close, each opening at or below the prior open, with strong bodies.
patterns.psychology: Sellers showed up three sessions in a row and closed near the lows. Buying pressure is absent.
patterns.signal: Bearish continuation or reversal confirmation.
patterns.entry: Below the third candle low, or on a bounce that fails at the first candle midpoint.
confirmation: volume stays above average across the three candles
no long lower wicks
patterns.false_signal: Three strong down candles into support can be capitulation. Shorting the third close is late.
patterns.notes: Best after a distribution top or a failed rally, not after a long extended decline.

patterns.name: Three Inside Up
patterns.structure: First two candles form a bullish harami; the third candle is bullish and closes above the first candle open.
patterns.psychology: The harami showed sellers losing control; the third candle confirms buyers have taken over.
patterns.signal: Bullish reversal with confirmation.
patterns.entry: Above the third candle high.
confirmation: third candle closes above the first candle open
volume expands on the third candle
patterns.false_signal: If the third candle closes back inside the first body, the confirmation failed.
patterns.notes: A harami plus a confirmation candle. Stronger than the harami alone.

patterns.name: Three Inside Down
patterns.structure: First two candles form a bearish harami; the third candle is bearish and closes below the first candle open.
patterns.psychology: The harami showed buyers losing control; the third candle confirms sellers have taken over.
patterns.signal: Bearish reversal with confirmation.
patterns.entry: Below the third candle low.
confirmation: third candle closes below the first candle open
volume expands on the third candle
patterns.false_signal: If the third candle closes back inside the first body, the confirmation failed.
patterns.notes: A harami plus a confirmation candle. Stronger than the harami alone.

patterns.name: Three Outside Up
patterns.structure: First two candles form a bullish engulfing; the third candle is bullish and closes above the engulfing close.
patterns.psychology: The engulfing showed buyers reversing the prior session; the third candle confirms the reversal.
patterns.signal: Bullish reversal with confirmation.
patterns.entry: Above the third candle high.
confirmation: third candle closes above the engulfing close
volume expands on the third candle
patterns.false_signal: If the third candle closes below the engulfing open, the confirmation failed.
patterns.notes: An engulfing plus a confirmation candle. One of the stronger three-candle reversal structures.

patterns.name: Three Outside Down
patterns.structure: First two candles form a bearish engulfing; the third candle is bearish and closes below the engulfing close.
patterns.psychology: The engulfing showed sellers reversing the prior session; the third candle confirms the reversal.
patterns.signal: Bearish reversal with confirmation.
patterns.entry: Below the third candle low.
confirmation: third candle closes below the engulfing close
volume expands on the third candle
patterns.false_signal: If the third candle closes above the engulfing open, the confirmation failed.
patterns.notes: An engulfing plus a confirmation candle. One of the stronger three-candle reversal structures.

patterns.name: Bullish Abandoned Baby
patterns.structure: First candle bearish; second candle is a doji that gaps below the first candle low; third candle bullish and gaps above the doji, closing above the first body midpoint.
patterns.psychology: Sellers gapped price down, but the doji showed exhaustion. Buyers then gapped price back up, leaving the sellers stranded.
patterns.signal: Strong bullish reversal after a decline.
patterns.entry: Above the third candle high.
confirmation: third candle closes above the first body midpoint
volume expands on the third candle
patterns.false_signal: Rare. If the gaps fill immediately, the pattern failed.
patterns.notes: A morning star with gaps on both sides of the doji. The gaps are the distinguishing feature.

patterns.name: Bearish Abandoned Baby
patterns.structure: First candle bullish; second candle is a doji that gaps above the first candle high; third candle bearish and gaps below the doji, closing below the first body midpoint.
patterns.psychology: Buyers gapped price up, but the doji showed exhaustion. Sellers then gapped price back down, leaving the buyers stranded.
patterns.signal: Strong bearish reversal after an advance.
patterns.entry: Below the third candle low.
confirmation: third candle closes below the first body midpoint
volume expands on the third candle
patterns.false_signal: Rare. If the gaps fill immediately, the pattern failed.
patterns.notes: An evening star with gaps on both sides of the doji. The gaps are the distinguishing feature.

patterns.name: Tri-Star
patterns.structure: Three consecutive dojis.
patterns.psychology: The market has stalled for three sessions. Neither side can hold a close.
patterns.signal: Strong indecision. Wait for the range to break.
patterns.entry: Break of the three-candle high or low.
patterns.stop: Other side of the three-candle range.
confirmation: next candle closes outside the three-candle range
volume expands on the break
patterns.false_signal: A tri-star in a quiet range is noise. The break often fails.
patterns.notes: Rare. Treat it as a compression marker, not a directional signal.
